# `Q-10-6` — Unknown Pipe

> A template applied a pipe name the engine does not
> recognize.

## What this means

Pandoc-flavored templates apply transformations through pipes:
`$name/uppercase$` runs `name` through the `uppercase` pipe,
`$x/left 10$` pads `x` to width 10 with left alignment, and so
on. This error fires when the pipe name does not match any
pipe the engine knows about. The template's strict-mode setting
determines whether the diagnostic is a warning or an error;
either way, the variable's value is passed through unchanged.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A typo in the pipe name** (`$x/uppercas$`).
- **A pipe from a different template engine** (Liquid, Jinja,
  Handlebars) that does not exist in Pandoc templates.
- **A pipe that was removed or renamed** between Quarto
  versions.

## How to fix

Replace the pipe with one that exists. The Pandoc template
documentation lists the available pipes; common ones include
`uppercase`, `lowercase`, `pairs`, `length`, `left`, `right`,
`center`, `alpha`, `roman`.

## Related

- `Q-10-7` — pipe arguments were invalid: the same family of
  pipe errors, but the pipe itself was recognized.
